newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up on peso, bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up on peso, bargain hunting.

text.p: Mexican stocks held on to midsession gains to close up for the second successive session Thursday as traders bought moderately and selectively due to relative peso stability and bargain prices, traders said.

"The market responded well, I would even say it looks solid as it fell at thin volume and rebounded in more vigorous trading. The peso settling down today definitely helped," said Carlos Samano, research director at the Bancomer brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 25.46 points, or 0.78 percent, at 3,288.47 points. Volume was regular at 65 million shares traded.

Traders said local and foreign delears stepped in to pick up attractively priced shares, but selectively and cautiously. Gains on the Dow Jones, helped, but traders were more concerned over local factors.

"Many prices were at support levels after the recent slide, which dealers realised and demand picked up. The market is complicated because volume is still mediocre and movements can still be manipulated," said a floor trader.

Financial stocks featured widely on the gainers list, headed by GFMulti B series shares, up 10 centavos (1 cent) to 1.10 pesos (14 cents), and Banacci B and L series in third and fourth places, up 84 centavos (11 cents) and 74 centavos (10 cents), respectively, to 17.68 ($2.29) and 16.50 pesos ($2.14).
The 48-hour peso ended 6.2 centavos firmer at 7.723.
"The financial sector's earnings reports will be good, in general. Most have slowed down the rate at which past-due loans are growing," a broker said.
Technical analysts said the IPC still showed signs of gaining and was trying to break a resistance at 3,300 points.
